subject: Recap: Copperline discovery — token heatmap & budget asks
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@copperline.com>, Tom Hsu <thsu@copperline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Copperline discovery — token heatmap & budget asks

Hi Alicia / Tom — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and explicit next steps so we’re all aligned. I’ve bolded the asks we need to move the pilot forward.

Key pain points you shared
- Monthly spend is spiking unpredictably when customers submit long statements (peak tokens per request).
- 99th percentile latency is impacting SLA for realtime underwriting flows.
- Current budget envelope for model spending is ~ $40k/month — finance will not exceed that without a clear TCO path.

Goals we heard
- Reduce per-request spend while keeping latency < 300ms (p50/p90 targets tighter than today).
- Proof that batching + KV/prefix caching will materially reduce token consumption for long-context requests.
- A short pilot (4–6 weeks) that demonstrates 30–50% cost reduction and preserves quality for the underwriting prompts.

Preliminary cost/TCO notes (back-of-envelope)
- You mentioned ~1.2M API calls / month and average observed input+output ~1,200 tokens.
- Baseline hosted run (current pattern) ~1.44B tokens/mo. At current list rates that’s in the ~$55–65k/month range (depends on model mix).
- If we apply batching + KV caching for repeated prefix content and use our optimized quantized variant, we estimate a 35–45% token reduction (example: prefixed sections compressed via KV -> fewer tokens sent each call). That would bring token consumption down to ~0.8–0.9B tokens -> estimated ~$30–38k/month.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU) pilot configurations can further reduce unit cost; rough pilot pricing shown in attached proforma.

Immediate asks (please):
1) Confirm the 1.2M calls/month and current average tokens per call (input + output). If you have a 7-day sample CSV that’s ideal.
2) Who in Finance and Legal should we include for pilot approvals and an NDA (Timelines depend on that).
3) Can you do a 60–90 minute sandbox session next week where we walk through the actual logs and test a 1k-request batching scenario?

Attachments: Copperline_Pilot_Proforma.xlsx (spreadsheet, 65KB) — contains pilot sizing, cost comparisons (hosted vs dedicated), and a 6-week runbook.

Next steps from Redwood side
- I’ll share a lightweight proforma (attached) and a proposed pilot SOW template.
- Marissa will pull model/quantization options and a short ROI calc for common batching outcomes.

Thanks again — I’ll wait on the volume confirmation and the sandbox availability.

—
Jonas Weber

Jonas — appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications and answers inline.

- Volume: confirmed ~1.2M requests/month (production underwriting flow).
- Tokens: our telemetry shows median ~450 tokens, but heavy tails push the average to ~1,200 when we include rich documents and OCR output. We can pull a 7-day sample; I’ve asked infra to export CSV.
- Budget: correct — finance has given us an active cap of $40k/month for model/API spend. Anything above needs a director-level sign-off.

Short asks from our side:
- Can you show a direct comparison (same prompt set) of: hosted baseline cost vs. batching+caching optimized cost? Numbers plus expected latency impact.
- We need a security/data residency check before starting any pilot with production data — can you kick off the questionnaire?

Looping in Tom (ops) and our procurement contact Maria Lopez (maria.lopez@copperline.com) — Maria will handle SOW and contracting timelines.

Available for the sandbox session next Tue (6/29) or Wed (6/30) mornings PT.

Thanks — Alicia

Forwarding Alicia’s confirms — quick internal notes: 

- Model choices: for long-context, recommend our Redwood-v2-small-quant (good latencies, quantized cost savings) or Redwood-v1-std for higher-quality passes. We can A/B within pilot.
- Ops levers: batching (dynamic batching window tuned to 50–200ms), prefix/KV caching for repeated claim text, and output length ceilings with constrained sampling for non-critical fields. Combined these typically hit the 30–50% token reduction band.
- Commercial: suggest we offer a pilot credit to bridge the first month to fit their $40k cap — propose 30% credit on pilot infrastructure + 2-week evaluation period. This makes the financial ask to Copperline more palatable and shortens procurement friction.

Jonas — I can run a 2-slide ROI snapshot (1-page) and Ben can sketch the Dedicated pool sizing. Put together before the sandbox session.

Subject: Pilot proposal & next meeting — Copperline

Thanks all — quick update and concrete proposal based on the numbers Alicia confirmed.

1) Confirmed inputs (from Alicia)
- 1.2M requests / month
- Avg tokens ~1,200 (heavy tail)
- Budget cap: $40k/mo before additional approvals

2) High-level TCO comparison (conservative estimates)
- Baseline hosted (no batching/cache): ~1.44B tokens/mo -> estimated cost $58k/mo (model mix dependent).
- Optimized hosted (batching + KV caching + quantized variant): token consumption down ~40% -> ~0.86B tokens -> estimated cost $34k/mo. Quality impact: negligible on underwriting fields we care about (we’ll validate).
- Dedicated pilot (reserved capacity + batching): higher fixed infra but lower per-token unit cost; estimated customer cash outlay after pilot credit: ~$12k/mo for reserved infra + nominal per-token usage fees (~$4–8k) = net ~$16–20k/mo effective during pilot (see attached proforma).

3) Commercial bridging suggestion
- Redwood proposes a 30% pilot credit for month 1 (applied to infra charges) to keep the effective first-month spend within their $40k cap while demonstrating ~40% token savings.

4) Security / procurement
- We’ll kick off the security questionnaire immediately; Ben will own the data residency checklist and provide the SOC2 articulation.

5) Proposed next steps
- Sandbox session: Tue 2027-06-29 09:30–10:45 PT (proposed) — please confirm.
- I’ll attach the Pilot SOW draft (working version) and the proforma spreadsheet. Marissa & Ben will include the ROI snapshot and pilot sizing before the session.

Attachments: Copperline_Pilot_Proforma.xlsx (spreadsheet, 65KB); Pilot_SOW_Draft.docx (doc stub, 12KB — internal draft).

If that schedule works I’ll send calendar invites and loop procurement points for contracting timeline.
